dish: Bönnsch — the city's own cloudy top-fermented beer — with Halve Hahn
w: Bonn's own brewpub, pouring the naturally cloudy Bönnsch it has brewed for forty years — the beer is also the name of the Bonn dialect. Rhenish plates, a barrel-vault room and a beer garden by the Sterntor.

dish: Rheinischer Sauerbraten with almond-raisin sauce and potato dumplings
w: A gasthaus on the market square with a tradition reaching back to 1389 — Bonn's oldest — and the address for uncompromisingly Rhenish cooking: Sauerbraten, Halve Hahn and Reibekuchen. Summer terrace right on the Markt.
A central brewery-restaurant serving hearty Rhenish home cooking — Reibekuchen, Sauerbraten and Brauhaus plates — in a relaxed city-centre gasthaus.

dish: classic Rhenish cooking in a Bonn-Republic institution
w: Founded 1931, the Bad Godesberg restaurant and Weinhaus that was the canteen of the Bonn Republic — every US president from Truman to Reagan, plus de Gaulle and Gorbachev, dined in its wood-panelled rooms under legendary host Ria Maternus.

dish: modern French tasting menu (one Michelin star)
w: Bonn's flagship gourmet address, a Michelin-starred kitchen in a Wilhelminian villa in Bad Godesberg turning out refined modern French cooking. A star holder for many years running.

dish: Japanese omakase menu, 4–6 courses (one Michelin star)
w: A Michelin-starred Japanese fine-dining room on the top floor of the Kameha Grand with sweeping Rhine views, chef Christian Sturm-Willms plating a contemporary omakase and one of Germany's deepest sake lists.
A beach-house-styled Michelin Guide restaurant in the Altstadt since 2000, doing fresh, seasonal Mediterranean plates in a maritime, laid-back setting.

dish: modern regional tasting menu with a deep wine list
w: A Michelin Guide restaurant and wine bar (two Hauben) in the former gardener's cottage of the La Redoute ballhouse, where chef Matthias Pietsch marries regional produce with international finesse.

dish: Italian specialities with a Rhine-terrace view
w: The Michelin Guide Italian in the AMERON Hotel Königshof, right on the Rhine promenade — polished Italian cooking with river views from the room and terrace.

dish: contemporary Mediterranean seafood and market plates, 17 floors up
address: Platz der Vereinten Nationen 4, 53113 Bonn, Germany
w: A Michelin-Plate restaurant and skybar on the 17th floor of the Bonn Marriott, floor-to-ceiling windows over the city, doing modern Mediterranean-leaning cooking.

The Michelin-starred riverside room of brothers Felix and Lukas Kaspar (star from 2017) closed permanently at year's end, citing chronic gastronomy staff shortages. Listed for the record; no longer operating.

dish: German and Mediterranean dining inside a hilltop castle
w: Dining in the ruins of the Godesburg, in Gottfried Böhm's 1960 building, with a knight's hall, bar and terrace high above Bad Godesberg — German and Mediterranean cooking with a Siebengebirge view.

dish: classic German cooking on a historic Rhine terrace
w: The Gobelin restaurant of an 1894 Art-Nouveau grand hotel on the Bad Godesberg riverfront, still run by the founding family — classic German cuisine and one of Bonn's finest Rhine terraces.

dish: self-service wholefood vegetarian and vegan buffet with vegan cakes
w: A Bonn institution opposite the Hauptbahnhof: a big self-service wholefood buffet, cooked in-house from largely organic produce for over three decades, now largely vegan, with cakes and ice cream too.

dish: hummus, falafel, fattoush and shakshuka with fresh pita
w: A small, colourful Nordstadt spot for Israeli/Levantine cooking — the hummus, freshly baked pita and shakshuka draw a devoted following. One of the highest-rated tables in the city.

dish: breakfast and brunch in a former swimming-pool hall
w: A relaxed student-and-professor favourite set in the entrance hall of a former swimming pool, doing breakfast, brunch, pasta, salads and cake all day. Named among the city's best breakfast cafés by the General-Anzeiger.

dish: all-day breakfast and Mediterranean small plates
w: A long-running city-centre café doing generous all-day breakfast, tapas, bowls and Mediterranean plates from morning to late — a General-Anzeiger pick for breakfast and brunch.

dish: single-origin filter coffee from an in-house roastery
w: A small specialty roastery-café in Beuel, founded 2013 alongside the Bonner Kaffeeschule barista academy — freshly roasted single origins as espresso and filter, plus beans to take home.

dish: Herrentorte layer cake and Christmas Stollen
w: A famed traditional Konditorei in a 1731 half-timbered house at the foot of the Drachenfels, run by the Profittlich family since 1892 and known far beyond the region for its Herrentorte and Stollen — a fine stop on the Drachenfels day-trip.
